nodes.name: Nickel foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: The 1×2 cm foam nickel substrate was immersed in a 200 mL solution containing 36 g Na2CO3, 4 g NaOH, and 1 g Na3PO4. The mixture was subjected to the 70°C water more than 5 min to remove any surface oil stains. Subsequently, the foam nickel substrate with free of oil stains were placed in diluted sulfuric acid to eliminate surface oxides. Then, the sample was thoroughly cleaned by rinsing it multiple times with anhydrous ethanol, ensuring a neutral pH of 7. Finally, the sample was stored in anhydrous ethanol for preservation.

nodes.name: HEA electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: NiFeCuCoCe-HEA was electrodeposited onto the nickel foam substrate using constant current. Briefly, nickel sulfate, copper sulfate, cobalt sulfate, ferrous sulfate, cerium sulfate, and sodium citrate were dissolved separately in different beakers. The solutions were then heated in a water bath at 70 degrees Celsius to facilitate dissolution. The dissolved electrodeposition liquid was thoroughly stirred and mixed. Next, 4 g·L⁻¹ boric acid and 2 g·L⁻¹ sodium orthophosphate was introduced, resulting in a final electrodeposition liquid with a fixed volume of 200 mL and a pH of 7.5. The experimental setup utilized the CHi660E electrochemical workstation, consisted of three standard electrodes: a three-electrode system was established using a nickel foam substrate, with an Hg/HgO electrode serving as the reference electrode and a Pt electrode as the counter electrode. A constant current deposition was performed for 1 h with a current density of 200 mA·cm⁻². After the electrodeposition process, the samples were heated in an oven at 70°C for over 3 h as an additional treatment. The obtained sample was named HEA-NCFCC/NF.

nodes.name: Electrochemical self-reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The electrochemical self-reconstruction treatment of HEA-NCFCC/NF was introduced to enhance the catalytic performance and corrosion resistance. This was conducted via cyclic voltammetry in a 1 M KOH with scan rate of 100 mV·s⁻¹ and potential range of 0.3–0.7 (V vs.Hg/HgO).
nodes.source_text: 2.3. Preparation of HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA electrocatalysts The electrochemical self-reconstruction treatment of HEA-NCFCC/NF was introduced... The resulted sample was named as HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA.

Under overpotentials of 219 mV, 266 mV and 295 mV, the HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA demonstrated current densities of 10 mA·cm−2, 100 mA·cm−2, and 200 mA·cm−2, respectively... the Tafel slope of HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA was 110.0 mV·dec−1... HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA had the largest double layer capacitance (79.8 mF·cm−2)... the FE of HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA was 96.48 %.

nodes.description: OER stability test at 50 mA/cm2 in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The stability of HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA was evaluated during 100 h of OER was evaluated using chronopotentiometry at a constant current density of 50 mA·cm−2. As depicted in the Fig. 4(f), the HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA exhibited minimal potential fluctuation during the entire test period, indicating excellent stability.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-NCFCC/NF displays prominent peaks at (111), (200), and (220) indicating distinct FCC crystalline nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 1(a), the HEANCFCC/NF displayed prominent peaks at (111), (200), and (220), indicating its distinct FCC crystalline nature.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA displays peaks at 465 cm⁻¹, 540 cm⁻¹, 660 cm⁻¹ (M-OOH), 563 cm⁻¹ (Fe-OH), 495 cm⁻¹ (Co-OOH) confirming presence of Fe-OOH and Co-OOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA displayed prominent peaks at 465 cm⁻¹, 540 cm⁻¹ and 660 cm⁻¹ corresponded to M-OOH [30,31], the peak at 563 cm⁻¹ corresponded to Fe-OH [32], as well as the peak at 495 cm⁻¹ corresponded to Co-OOH [33].

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA exhibits peaks at 3500 cm⁻¹, 1597 cm⁻¹, and 1088 cm⁻¹ due to vibrations of M-OH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA after reconstruction exhibited prominent peaks at 3500 cm⁻¹, 1597 cm⁻¹, and 1088 cm⁻¹, which can be due to the vibrations of M-OH.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-NCFCC/NF shows uneven granular flake-like structures. HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA exhibits uniformly distributed lamellar structure of stacked nanosheets increasing specific surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As depicted in Fig. 2 (a-b), the HEA-NCFCC/NF exhibited an uneven distribution of granular structures... after electrochemical self-reconstruction, the surface exhibited a uniformly distributed lamellar structure...

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-NCFCC/NF shows crystal spacings of 0.217 nm (111) and 0.213 nm (111). HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA shows layered structure with spacings of 0.216 nm (111) and 0.179 nm (220).
nodes.evidence_snippet: HRTEM images of HEA-NCFCC/NF revealed a crystal spacing of 0.217 nm corresponding to (111) and 0.213 nm... HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA exhibited... crystal face spacing of 0.216 nm and 0.179 nm primarily attributed to the (111) and (220) crystal face...

nodes.characterization_summary: Even distribution of Ni, Fe, Cu, Co, and Ce elements on HEA-NCFCC/NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX mapping of HEA-NCFCC/NF resulted in Fig. 2(k) demonstrated the even distribution of Ni, Fe, Cu, Co and Ce elements on the sample surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-NCFCC/NF composition: 20.98% Ni, 25.53% Fe, 26.89% Co, 20.60% Cu, 6.00% Ce.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based on ICP-OES in Table S1, the plating of HEA-NCFCC/NF catalyst consisted of 20.98% Ni, 25.53% Fe, 26.89% Co, 20.60% Cu and 6.00% Ce.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p: HEA-NCFCC/NF shows Ni⁰ (852.0 eV), Ni²⁺ (855.9, 873.83 eV); HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA shows additional Ni³⁺ (858.10 eV). Fe, Co, Cu show shifts to higher valence states after reconstruction confirming Ni/Fe/Co-OOH formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fig. 3(a) Ni 2p XPS spectrum of HEA-NCFCC/NF... the peak at 852.0 eV corresponds to the Ni⁰ valence state... After the electrochemical self-reconstruction, the HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA exhibited a new weak peak at 858.10 eV... XPS findings confirmed the successful formation of Ni/Fe/Co-OOH.

nodes.evidence_snippet: HEA-NCFCC/NF@EA had the largest double layer capacitance (79.8 mF·cm⁻²).
